presentation_title: Mastering Prompts: The 3 C's and Example-Driven AI Interaction
episode: 2.1 The Anatomy of a Good Prompt
learning_objectives: Understand the importance of Clarity, Context, and Constraints in prompt writing.
Learn how to apply the '3 C's' to improve prompt effectiveness.
Discover the power of providing a 'Persona' to the AI.
Differentiate between Zero-Shot, One-Shot, and Few-Shot prompting techniques.
outline: The 3 C's of Prompt Writing: Clarity, Context, Constraints
Understanding Zero-Shot, One-Shot, and Few-Shot Prompting
prerequisites: Basic understanding of how to interact with AI chat models (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini).

slides.title: Welcome: The Anatomy of a Good Prompt
content: Weak prompts lead to weak answers.
Great prompts lead to great answers.
Learn to craft effective prompts.
slides.narration: Hello learners! Welcome to this episode on 'The Anatomy of a Good Prompt'. Have you asked an AI a question? Was the answer not what you expected? It's likely the prompt was not effective. A chef needs good ingredients for a great meal. An AI needs a great prompt for a great answer. Today, we'll craft prompts for desired results.

An open mind to experiment and learn.

slides.title: The Power of a Good Prompt
content: Your prompt is the AI's instruction manual.
A weak prompt = a weak, generic answer.
A great prompt = a specific, helpful answer.
slides.narration: Think of your prompt as the AI's instruction manual. Vague instructions lead to generic outputs. The AI tries its best, but results may be unhelpful. Clear instructions help the AI deliver amazing results. The output will be useful. It's all about communicating your needs. What makes a good instruction manual?
slides.image_prompt: A split image: on one side, a confused person looking at a generic, unhelpful AI response; on the other, a smiling person looking at a specific, helpful AI response. An arrow points from 'weak prompt' to 'weak answer' and 'strong prompt' to 'strong answer'.

slides.title: Introducing The 3 C's: Clarity, Context, Constraints
content: Clarity: Be specific about what you want.
Context: Provide background information.
Constraints: Set rules for the output.
slides.narration: Good prompts have three key ingredients. We call these 'The 3 C's'. They are Clarity, Context, and Constraints. These elements guide the AI. They help generate the perfect response. Let's break down each one individually.
slides.image_prompt: Three distinct icons arranged in a triangle: a magnifying glass for Clarity, a thought bubble/speech bubble for Context, and a ruler or boundary lines for Constraints.

slides.title: Clarity: Be Specific!
content: The AI doesn't know what you're thinking.
Vague prompts lead to generic answers.
Specific prompts yield specific, helpful outputs.
slides.narration: First up is Clarity. This means being specific! The AI cannot read your mind. Vague input leads to vague answers. The AI won't know your exact needs. Specificity helps the AI tailor its response. It meets your needs better.
slides.image_prompt: A large magnifying glass hovering over a piece of text that starts blurry and becomes sharp, illustrating the concept of specificity. An icon of a thought bubble with a question mark inside.

slides.title: Clarity: Weak Prompt Example
content: Weak Prompt: "Write about electric cars."
What do you think the AI will generate?
Likely a general overview.
slides.narration: Let's look at a weak prompt. If you simply say: "Write about electric cars." What kind of output do you expect? The AI might give a history. It could list models or a general description. It's too broad, isn't it? The AI must guess your interest in electric cars.
slides.image_prompt: A generic illustration of an electric car. A screen displaying the prompt 'Write about electric cars.' and a very broad, unspecific AI response.

slides.title: Clarity: Good Prompt Example
content: Good Prompt (Clear): "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
See how much more detail is added?
This guides the AI much better.
slides.narration: Let's make that prompt clearer. We want a short blog post. It explains top 3 benefits of owning an electric car. This is for a city resident. Notice the difference? We specified format, number of benefits, and topic. Also, we added the target audience. This is a much clearer instruction for the AI.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of an electric car being charged in a city environment. A screen displaying the improved prompt with specific details highlighted.

slides.title: Clarity: Weak vs. Good
content: Weak: "Write about electric cars." -> Generic overview.
Good: "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city." -> Focused, useful content.
The more specific, the better the output.
slides.narration: Compare the two. The weak prompt is a generic overview. The good prompt gives focused, useful content. It is relevant to a specific scenario. What do you notice here? The good prompt reduces AI guessing. It gives a more precise and helpful response. Always aim for specificity!
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison of two AI chat outputs: one is a generic paragraph about electric cars from the weak prompt, the other is a structured blog post about city electric car benefits from the good prompt. A 'before and after' visual.

slides.title: Context: Give it Background!
content: Context tells the AI 'why' you're asking.
Helps the AI adopt the right perspective.
Ensures the output fits your situation.
slides.narration: Next is Context. This provides background information to the AI. Why are you asking this question? Who is the audience for the output? Context helps the AI understand the situation. It adopts the right perspective. The AI tailors its response to your needs. It also considers your audience's needs.
slides.image_prompt: A person sketching a background scene for a character, symbolizing providing context. A thought bubble icon with information flowing into it.

slides.title: Context: Starting with a Clear Prompt
content: Let's start with our "Good Prompt (Clear)":
"Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
This is clear, but who is it for?
slides.narration: Let's use our clear prompt. It's about a blog post on electric car benefits. This targets city residents. This prompt is good and specific. We can improve it by adding context. Who is the target audience for this post? What type of blog is it for?
slides.image_prompt: A city skyline with an electric car. The existing good prompt is displayed on a screen.

slides.title: Context: Better Prompt Example
content: Better Prompt (with Context): "Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
We've added the target blog and its focus.
This helps the AI choose the right tone and angle.
slides.narration: We add context this way: Write a short blog post. It is for a lifestyle blog on sustainable living. Explain top 3 electric car benefits for city dwellers. The AI now knows its blog type and audience. This helps it choose tone and vocabulary. It also highlights relevant benefits.
slides.image_prompt: An image of a person reading a tablet displaying a lifestyle blog focused on sustainable living. The improved prompt, with the context highlighted, is shown on a screen.

slides.title: Context: Good vs. Better
content: Good: General blog post about benefits.
Better: Blog post tailored for a sustainable living audience.
Context ensures relevance and appropriate tone.
slides.narration: Think about the difference. The 'good' prompt gave a general blog post. The 'better' prompt is tailored for sustainable living. It might emphasize environmental benefits. Or it could focus on cost savings for eco-conscious people. What tone suits a sustainable living blog? Added context makes the output more relevant. It also engages the readers better.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison of two AI chat outputs: one is a general blog post, the other is a blog post with a clear sustainable living tone and focus. A visual representing 'audience' or 'target group'.

slides.title: Constraints: Set the Rules!
content: Constraints are boundaries that shape the output.
Tell the AI the length, format, and style you need.
Ensures the output meets your specific requirements.
slides.narration: Finally, we have Constraints. These are the rules you set for the AI's output. Do you need a certain length? In a specific format? With a particular writing style? Constraints help the AI deliver what you need. No extra fluff or missing elements.
slides.image_prompt: A graphic showing a ruler, a clock, and a style guide icon, representing length, time/duration, and style constraints. A person setting boundaries with ropes.

slides.title: Constraints: Building on Our Prompt
content: Let's use our "Better Prompt (with Context)":
"Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
What else can we specify?
slides.narration: We are building a super prompt! We have clarity and context. Now, let's use our 'Better Prompt'. It is a blog post for a sustainable living blog. It explains top 3 electric car benefits for city dwellers. What other rules can we add for precision?
slides.image_prompt: A partially complete blog post draft on a screen, with placeholders for more instructions. The 'Better Prompt' is displayed.

slides.title: Constraints: Excellent Prompt Example
content: Excellent Prompt (with Constraints): "Write a short blog post, under 400 words, for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city. Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone and end with a question to encourage comments."
We've added length, tone, and a specific ending.
This leaves no room for ambiguity.
slides.narration: Here is our 'Excellent Prompt'. It has added constraints. Write a short blog post, under 400 words. It is for a sustainable living blog. Explain top 3 electric car benefits for city residents. Use a friendly, enthusiastic tone. End with a question to encourage comments. The AI now knows the word count. It understands the desired tone. It also knows how to conclude the post. This is incredibly specific!
slides.image_prompt: A person typing on a laptop, with a word count visible on the screen and a small icon representing a friendly and enthusiastic tone (e.g., a smiling face). The 'Excellent Prompt' is displayed.

slides.title: Constraints: Better vs. Excellent
content: Better: Good content, but length/tone might vary.
Excellent: Content, length, tone, and engagement strategy all defined.
Constraints make the output truly fit your needs.
slides.narration: The 'better' prompt gave good content. But length and tone might vary. The 'excellent' prompt defines content, length, and tone. It even includes an engagement strategy. This output truly matches your vision. Notice the high level of specificity now.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison of two AI chat outputs: one is a blog post without specific length/tone, the other is a blog post under 400 words, with a friendly tone, and ending with a question. A visual showing a 'checklist' being completed.

slides.title: Recap: The 3 C's in Action
content: Clarity: Be specific about your request.
Context: Provide background and audience info.
Constraints: Set rules for format, length, and style.
Combine them for powerful prompts!
slides.narration: So, let's recap the 3 C's. Clarity means being specific. Context gives the AI background and audience info. Constraints set rules for format, length, and style. Combine these three for powerful prompts. They become incredibly effective!
slides.image_prompt: An infographic showing the three 'C's' (Clarity, Context, Constraints) interlinked or as parts of a single, strong prompt icon. A lightbulb illuminates the infographic.

slides.title: Bonus Tip: Provide a Persona
content: Tell the AI who to be.
Helps the AI adopt a specific voice and perspective.
Super-powerful for targeted responses.
slides.narration: Here's a bonus tip to supercharge your prompts. Provide a Persona! Tell the AI who you want it to act as. This helps the AI adopt a specific voice. It also sets the tone and perspective. Responses become more tailored and authentic.
slides.image_prompt: An icon of a theatrical mask, symbolizing 'persona'. A small thought bubble above it with different character traits.

slides.title: Persona: Example
content: Prompt: "Act as an expert travel agent specializing in budget travel. Create a 5-day itinerary for a trip to Rome for a solo traveler who loves history and food."
The AI will respond as if it's a travel agent.
The output will be relevant to budget travel.
slides.narration: For example: Act as an expert budget travel agent. Create a 5-day Rome itinerary for a solo traveler. This traveler loves history and food. Giving the AI this role sets its viewpoint. It will generate a budget-friendly itinerary. Just like a real budget travel agent would.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of a friendly travel agent sitting at a desk, talking to a client about a map of Rome. A laptop screen shows the prompt with the 'Act as...' part highlighted.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Zero, One, and Few-Shot Prompting
content: How you give examples to the AI.
Zero-Shot: No examples.
One-Shot: One example.
Few-Shot: A few examples.
slides.narration: Now, let's discuss another powerful technique. This involves giving the AI examples. This might sound technical, but it is simple. You give zero, one, or a few examples. This helps the AI understand your desired pattern or format.
slides.image_prompt: Three distinct icons: a '0' for Zero-Shot, a '1' for One-Shot, and a '3' (or multiple dots) for Few-Shot, arranged horizontally.

slides.title: Zero-Shot Prompting
content: You give zero examples.
Most prompts you write are Zero-Shot.
You just ask for what you want directly.
slides.narration: Zero-Shot prompting means no examples are given. You ask for what you want directly. All previous examples were Zero-Shot. They used the 3 C's and personas. You give instructions without an input-output pair.
slides.image_prompt: A blank canvas with a paintbrush, symbolizing starting from scratch without an example. A simple AI chat interface showing a direct question and answer.

slides.title: One-Shot Prompting
content: You give one example to show the AI a pattern.
Great for specific formatting or style.
AI learns from the single provided example.
slides.narration: One-Shot prompting gives the AI one example. It shows the exact pattern or format. This is useful for specific structures or styles. Words alone might not be enough.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of a single blueprint or template being presented to a robot or AI. A single example text box followed by an instruction to apply the format.

slides.title: One-Shot Prompting: Example
content: Prompt: "Summarize text into key points like this: Text: 'The sun is a star, and it's the center of our solar system.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'
"Now, use this format for the following text: [insert long article here]"
The AI now knows the exact output format.
slides.narration: Here is an example: Summarize text into key points. For instance, Text: 'The sun is a star, and it's the center of our solar system.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'. Now, apply this format to [insert long article here]. We gave one perfect example for the summary format. The AI will replicate this exact format. It will apply it to the new, longer article.
slides.image_prompt: A split screen showing the example 'Text: ... Output: ...' clearly, then an arrow pointing to a large text box labeled 'Long Article', implying the AI will apply the format to it. The example format is highlighted.

slides.title: Few-Shot Prompting
content: You give a few examples to teach a complex pattern.
Useful for more nuanced or varied tasks.
AI learns from multiple input-output pairs.
slides.narration: Few-Shot prompting goes a step further. You provide several examples to the AI. This teaches a complex pattern. Or it shows a range of desired outputs. It is great for nuanced tasks. The AI learns multiple response variations.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of three different blueprints or templates being presented to a robot or AI. Multiple example text boxes followed by an instruction to apply the pattern.

slides.title: Few-Shot Prompting: Example
content: Example 1: Text: 'Happy.' Sentiment: Positive.
Example 2: Text: 'Sad.' Sentiment: Negative.
Example 3: Text: 'Neither happy nor sad.' Sentiment: Neutral.
"Now, categorize the sentiment of the following text: [new text]"
AI learns the sentiment classification pattern.
slides.narration: Imagine categorizing sentiment with AI. Give three examples. Example 1: Text: 'Happy.' Sentiment: Positive. Example 2: Text: 'Sad.' Sentiment: Negative. Example 3: Text: 'Neither happy nor sad.' Sentiment: Neutral. Then, categorize sentiment for [new text]. Multiple examples teach the AI the full range of classification.
slides.image_prompt: A screen displaying three distinct text-sentiment pairs clearly. Below it, a new text box awaits sentiment classification, indicating the AI will apply the learned pattern.

slides.title: Review: Prompting Techniques Recap
content: The 3 C's (Clarity, Context, Constraints) are essential.
Providing a Persona enhances AI's voice.
Zero-Shot: Direct requests (no examples).
One-Shot: One example for specific formatting.
Few-Shot: Multiple examples for complex patterns.
slides.narration: Let's quickly review the key techniques. Remember the 3 C's: Clarity, Context, and Constraints are crucial for prompt writing. Providing a Persona enhances the AI's response voice. Zero-Shot, One-Shot, and Few-Shot describe example provision. These tools help create better AI interactions.
slides.image_prompt: An infographic summarizing the 3 C's, a mask for persona, and the 0, 1, few icons, similar to the summary slide but focused on review. A question mark icon for 'recap'.

slides.title: Summary: Key Takeaways
content: The 3 C's (Clarity, Context, Constraints) are essential for good prompts.
Providing a Persona enhances AI's voice and perspective.
Zero-Shot: Direct requests (no examples).
One-Shot: One example for specific formatting.
Few-Shot: Multiple examples for complex patterns.
slides.narration: Let's summarize what we have learned. Remember the 3 C's: Clarity, Context, and Constraints. These are your building blocks for powerful prompts. The bonus tip: a Persona improves AI responses greatly. You understand Zero, One, and Few-Shot prompting. You know when to use each for best results. What will you try first?

slides.title: Assignment: Practice Your Prompting Skills!
content: 1. Choose a simple topic (e.g., healthy eating, learning a new skill).
2. Write a 'Weak Prompt' for it.
3. Rewrite it, applying the '3 C's' to make it an 'Excellent Prompt'.
4. Add a 'Persona' to your excellent prompt.
5. Try a One-Shot prompt for a specific formatting task.
6. Compare the outputs from your weak and excellent prompts.
slides.narration: Now it's time to practice what you have learned! Choose a simple topic for your assignment. For instance, healthy eating or learning a new skill. First, write a 'Weak Prompt' for it. Then, rewrite it. Apply Clarity, Context, and Constraints. Make it an 'Excellent Prompt'. Add a 'Persona' to your excellent prompt! Finally, try a One-Shot prompt. Use it for a simple formatting task. Compare weak and excellent prompt outputs. You will be amazed by the difference!
slides.image_prompt: A person sitting at a laptop, actively typing, with a checklist on the screen. Icons representing 'weak' and 'excellent' prompts are shown side-by-side with comparison arrows.
